trials.notes: Used the correct Tag Processor for a flat class mutation and byte-preserving output. All API calls were documented: constructor, next_tag(), add_class(), and get_updated_html(). The while-loop plus get_updated_html() pattern is idiomatic, and the documented next_tag()/add_class() behavior covers uppercase tags, comments, existing classes, unquoted attributes, and incomplete trailing tags.

Identical implementation to trial-1. Correct processor choice, no undocumented methods, no _doing_it_wrong records, and idiomatic repeated next_tag('img') scanning with add_class() followed by get_updated_html().

Identical implementation to trial-1. The lowercase query is documented as ASCII case-insensitive, add_class() is documented to create or append without reordering existing classes, and get_updated_html() is the documented byte-preserving retrieval method.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well on the exact decision points this task required: the Tag Processor overview says to use it for flat class/attribute edits and byte-precise preservation; Finding tags documents next_tag('img'); next_tag() explicitly says tag-name matching is ASCII case-insensitive, comments/raw text are not matched, and truncated tags are not modified; add_class() documents creating class attributes, appending to existing classes, preserving existing order, and no-op duplicate behavior; get_updated_html() is clearly documented as the way to retrieve queued edits while preserving untouched bytes. Near-miss: the trial explanations did not explicitly mention incomplete input, but their chosen documented API handled it correctly because incomplete trailing tags are never matched and untouched bytes are preserved.

doc_gaps.problem: The method says it creates a class attribute when absent, but the placement rule for that newly created attribute is only documented under set_attribute().
doc_gaps.suggestion: Cross-reference the attribute placement contract from add_class(): when a class attribute is created, it is inserted using the same new-attribute placement rules, while existing class attributes keep their position.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs show single-match examples more prominently than the common repeated-edit loop, even though repeated scanning is the main pattern for modifying every matching tag.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a generic example showing `while ( $processor->next_tag( $tag_name ) ) { ... }` followed by `get_updated_html()` for applying the same attribute or class edit to all matches.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs state incomplete trailing tags are not matched, and get_updated_html() separately states untouched bytes are preserved, but the combined consequence is not made explicit at the truncation note.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one sentence that if an incomplete trailing token is not matched or modified, `get_updated_html()` will leave those original trailing bytes unchanged.
